A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same ReasonEmbed study with ReMixer and Redapter. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-C are readable and matchable across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original BRIGHT and R2MED retrieval experiments, component ablations, data-scaling results, and contamination analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds annotation-quality evaluation, retriever sensitivity, runtime measurements, and general-retrieval experiments.

M1.justification: The ReMixer pipeline, distilled annotator, and Redapter weighting procedure are unchanged. V2's explanation of positive/negative label thresholds restates information already shown in v1 Figure 1. Alternative candidate retrievers are tested as ablations without replacing the default method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds non-reasoning-intensive retrieval evaluation on TREC-COVID and KAPR, substantially extending the task coverage beyond BRIGHT and R2MED. Natural Questions, previously cited but not experimentally used, now supplies training data for a comparator. The original synthetic training corpus is retained.

E2.justification: The main BRIGHT and R2MED comparator rosters are unchanged. New targeted comparisons include an NQ-trained Qwen3-8B model, Qwen3-Embedding-4B and BGE-M3 as alternative candidate miners, and direct teacher/zero-shot comparisons for annotation quality (Tables 4, 5, 10, and 12).

E3.justification: V2 introduces held-out annotation evaluation on 60,000 pairs and human validation on 360 pairs by three authors, ROUGE overlap measurements, and controlled candidate-miner comparisons. Appendix C.4 compares 58,568 NQ training examples with three synthetic-data sizes. Tables 2-3 also correct Qwen3-4B-ms from 8B to 4B; this reporting correction does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands pipeline validation through direct annotation-quality assessment (Section 5.3), lexical-overlap diagnostics of triviality (Section 5.4.1), sensitivity to the initial retriever (Appendix A.2), and training-cost analysis (Appendix B.3). The earlier component ablations, scaling analysis, and contamination checks remain.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 newly reports Cohen's kappa as a chance-corrected statistical assessment of annotation agreement with the teacher. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests, so the addition does not establish improved uncertainty reporting for retrieval performance.

E6.justification: Main retrieval and existing ablation scores are retained, including Qwen3-8B's BRIGHT/R2MED averages of 38.1/43.18. New outcomes include kappa 0.6001 versus 0.4314, distilled/teacher annotation accuracy of 85.0%/86.1%, alternative-miner BRIGHT scores of 37.2 and 35.9, ROUGE measurements, runtimes, and TREC-COVID/KAPR scores (Tables 4, 5, 7, and 10-12). These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Candidate selection, InfoNCE, the clipped reasoning-intensity ratio, and batch normalization retain their mathematical definitions. V2 displays the previously inline reasoning-intensity definition as Equation 2 and renumbers subsequent equations; no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three contributions and the headline BRIGHT score of 38.1. The added introduction reference to the triviality analysis supplies evidence for an existing claim rather than redefining it.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning transfer to ordinary retrieval, robustness to weaker candidate miners, and low training overhead; the existing limitations remain. It also corrects DIVER's description from 'strongest' to 'competitive': Table 3 reports RaDeR at 35.19 versus DIVER at 32.23 in both versions.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1 and A.3 newly disclose SGLang inference, while Appendix B.3 reports 1,304 training steps and runtimes of 13,144 seconds for contrastive learning and 13,378 seconds for Redapter. Core hyperparameters, prompts, hardware, licenses, and promised resource access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for KAPR (Capari et al., 2024), TREC-COVID (Voorhees et al., 2021), and SGLang (Zheng et al., 2024a). The related-work discussion and positioning of the central contributions are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: V2 adds an annotation-quality research question and section, appendix subsections for runtime and general retrieval, and acknowledgments. It makes localized wording, explanatory, and cross-reference edits while retaining most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence.

P2.justification: V2 adds six compact result tables (4, 5, 7, and 10-12), relocates existing displays as text flows, and gives reasoning intensity a numbered equation. The three original figures and established table designs are retained; appendix prompt captions receive small corrections.

improvement.justification: V1 supported annotation quality mainly through downstream retrieval; v2 adds direct teacher agreement on 60,000 pairs and author judgments on 360 pairs. Together with lexical-overlap diagnostics, retriever sensitivity, and runtime analysis, this substantially strengthens evidence for the central synthesis and training pipeline. The general-retrieval comparison remains limited by unequal training-data sizes and an unnamed metric in Table 12, but these limitations do not outweigh the validation gains.
